notes_on_local_grants: On the LOCAL Postgres (via _local_stubs.sql), the 'authenticated' role has no default table GRANTs, so the RLS test also had to run: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public + GRANT ALL ON ALL TABLES/SEQUENCES to authenticated. This is NOT an issue in real Supabase because Supabase pre-grants privileges on public to the authenticated/anon roles via ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES. No change needed in migration.sql — only mentioning for context so the next testing agent doesn't get confused by 'permission denied' during local runs.
critical_code_review_comments: migration.sql: helper functions is_member/can_write reference tables created later; the added 'set check_function_bodies = off' at the top is the correct fix and works.
set_invoice_no / set_quotation_no are cleanly separated per-table trigger functions — good fix over the shared set_doc_no crash.
next_number() correctly uses counters.value in ON CONFLICT / RETURNING.

The migration relies on Supabase's default GRANTs for the authenticated role. Consider adding explicit 'grant usage on schema public to authenticated, anon;' and 'grant select/insert/update/delete on all tables in schema public to authenticated;' at the end of migration.sql to be defensive against non-standard projects and to make the file portable to any Postgres/Supabase project.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The reported bug ('relation public.project_members does not exist') is fully fixed. Migration is idempotent. Smoke SQL passes end-to-end. Frontend auth works and correctly shows the branded setup-required screen because the user's real Supabase project has not yet had migration.sql applied. If retesting locally, remember to GRANT privileges to the authenticated role after loading _local_stubs.sql because Supabase's default GRANTs are not simulated by the stubs.
rca of the issue: Root cause was helper SQL functions (is_member/can_write) referencing public.project_members inside their bodies while the CREATE FUNCTION statements ran BEFORE project_members was created. Postgres validates function bodies at creation time by default (check_function_bodies=on) and raised 42P01. Fix: 'set check_function_bodies = off;' near top of migration.sql defers body validation until execution time, by which point all referenced tables exist. Two related fixes were also applied: next_number()'s ON CONFLICT/RETURNING was corrected to use counters.value, and the shared set_doc_no trigger (which crashed with 'record new has no field invoice_no' when attached to quotations) was split into dedicated set_invoice_no() and set_quotation_no() functions. All three fixes verified working.
